title: Career Roadmap: Journalist
summary: A Journalist researches, verifies and reports news and information to help the public understand events, developments and issues. Journalists work across newspapers, news websites, television, radio, podcasts and independent media platforms.

facts.Current degree: Liberal Arts / Liberal Studies – Politics, Philosophy & Economics (PPE)

about.label: Primary Industries
about.text: Print Media, Digital News, Television, Radio, Investigative Media, Documentary Production

about.label: Suitable For
about.text: Students interested in current affairs, politics, economics, public issues, research, writing and storytelling

blocks.text: A Journalist researches, verifies and reports news and information to help the public understand events, developments and issues. Journalists work across newspapers, news websites, television, radio, podcasts and independent media platforms.

A Politics, Philosophy & Economics (PPE) background can be particularly valuable for political reporting, economic journalism, public policy coverage and investigative reporting because it develops critical thinking and an understanding of institutions, arguments and economic systems.
Key responsibilities

items.text: Identify newsworthy events, issues and emerging stories.
Research topics using reliable sources and public records.
Interview experts, officials, community members and eyewitnesses.
Verify facts, quotations, images and documents.
Write news reports, explainers, features and investigative stories.
Analyse political, economic and social developments.
Follow editorial standards, media ethics and applicable laws.
Publish or present stories across print, digital, audio and video formats.

blocks.label: Example
blocks.text: During a major economic policy announcement, a journalist examines the policy, interviews economists and affected communities, checks official documents and explains how the changes may affect citizens and businesses.
Undergraduate route
BA / Liberal Arts – Politics, Philosophy & Economics (PPE)
Develop knowledge of political institutions, economic systems, public policy, reasoning, research and social issues.
Journalism and media fundamentals
Learn news writing, interviewing, fact-checking, media law, ethics, editing and reporting techniques through electives, workshops or practical training.
Practical newsroom experience
Build a portfolio through a student publication, campus newspaper, digital news project, podcast or internship.
Further study options
Depending on the student's interests and admission eligibility, consider:

items.text: MA Journalism and Mass Communication
MA Journalism
MA Political Communication
Postgraduate programmes in Broadcast or Digital Journalism
Specialised programmes in Investigative Journalism or Documentary Production
Courses in Data Journalism, Public Policy or Economic Journalism

blocks.text: A journalism postgraduate degree is not always mandatory. Many entry-level opportunities accept graduates from different disciplines who demonstrate strong writing, research, reporting and verification skills.
Year 1 — Build Knowledge and Writing Skills

items.text: Read news from multiple credible sources daily.
Study political systems, economics, philosophy and contemporary social issues.
Practise concise writing, grammar, summarisation and headline writing.
Learn the difference between news reporting, opinion and analysis.
Start a journal of potential story ideas.

blocks.label: Mini-project
blocks.text: Write five short news reports based on verified public information.
Year 2 — Learn Reporting and Verification

items.text: Practise interviews, source development and note-taking.
Learn fact-checking, reverse-image verification and source evaluation.
Study media ethics, defamation basics, privacy and reporting risks.
Develop skills in audio recording, photography and basic video editing.

blocks.label: Project
blocks.text: Produce a reported feature on a local community, education or public-policy issue using multiple sources.
Year 3 — Specialise and Publish

items.text: Choose an area such as politics, economics, business, environment or investigative journalism.
Learn data journalism using spreadsheets and public datasets.
Practise writing explainers, long-form features and interview-based stories.
Publish work through a student publication or a clearly labelled personal portfolio.

blocks.label: Project
blocks.text: Produce a data-supported story with documented sources, interviews and visualisations.
Final Year — Prepare for the Newsroom

items.text: Complete an internship with a newsroom, digital publisher or media organisation.
Develop a portfolio of strong, fact-checked published or unpublished work.
Practise news judgment, deadline writing and editing.
Learn multimedia storytelling and basic content management systems.
Apply for reporter, editorial assistant, research and trainee journalist roles.
Prepare for writing tests, current-affairs discussions and editorial interviews.

blocks.text: Political Journalist
Reports on elections, government, political parties, public policy and legislative developments.

blocks.label: Useful foundation
blocks.text: political science, governance, policy research and interviewing.
Business and Economic Journalist
Covers companies, budgets, economic policy, employment, markets and financial developments.

blocks.label: Useful foundation
blocks.text: economics, financial literacy, data interpretation and document analysis.
Investigative Journalist
Examines complex issues through sustained research, documents, interviews and corroborated evidence.

blocks.label: Useful foundation
blocks.text: persistence, public-record research, verification and ethical source handling.
Digital Journalist
Produces news for websites, mobile platforms, newsletters and social media.

blocks.label: Useful foundation
blocks.text: digital storytelling, multimedia production, audience analytics and SEO basics.
Data Journalist
Uses datasets, statistics and visualisations to explain trends and investigate public-interest questions.

blocks.label: Useful foundation
blocks.text: spreadsheets, statistics, data cleaning and visual storytelling.
Broadcast Journalist
Reports and presents news through television, radio, live coverage, podcasts or video formats.

blocks.label: Useful foundation
blocks.text: spoken communication, scripting, presentation and audio-video production.
A journalism portfolio should demonstrate accuracy, research depth, clarity, source diversity and the ability to explain why a story matters.

blocks.text: Look for opportunities with newspapers, news agencies, digital publishers, television channels, radio stations, independent investigative outlets and public-interest media organisations.
For each portfolio piece, clearly distinguish verified facts from analysis or opinion. Keep source notes, confirm quotations, seek responses from relevant parties and correct errors transparently.

rows.text: Spreadsheets, reference managers and structured source logs
Excel or Google Sheets, basic visualisation tools
Reverse-image search, metadata inspection where available, source triangulation
CapCut, DaVinci Resolve or equivalent editing tools
Content management systems and basic digital publishing workflows
Basic website analytics and social-platform metrics

blocks.text: Tools are secondary to strong reporting. Learn only those that support the type of journalism the student wants to pursue.

blocks.text: Prioritise training that includes practical assignments and feedback. A certificate does not substitute for published work, reliable reporting or professional judgment.

Other career paths include documentary production, editorial research, public-interest communications and media analysis. Career progression varies by organisation, expertise and the quality of a journalist's work.

items.text: Data-driven investigative journalism
AI-assisted research and newsroom workflows
Verification of AI-generated images, video and audio
Independent newsletters and niche digital publications
Podcasts and documentary storytelling
Climate, science and public-health journalism
Audience-focused explanatory journalism

blocks.text: AI can help organise information and support transcription, but journalists must independently verify claims, quotations and sources. Confidential sources and unpublished material should not be uploaded to unapproved AI systems.

Final Recommendation

For students pursuing Liberal Arts with a Politics, Philosophy & Economics (PPE) specialisation, journalism is a strong pathway for applying their understanding of governance, economics, institutions and society to real-world reporting.

Prioritise writing, interviewing, verification, research, media ethics and a demonstrable portfolio. PPE knowledge can provide a valuable subject-matter advantage, but consistent reporting practice and the ability to establish facts independently are what turn that foundation into professional journalistic capability.
